issues.legal_issue: An arbitration award that preserves existing securities over land without creating or declaring an interest in immovable property does not require registration.
material_facts: The award stated that existing documents relating to debts secured on land would remain as before and continue as security until payment.
The award also stated that the debtor would have no right to transfer the land, but the Court treated this as stating an existing fact rather than creating or declaring an interest in the land.
The award was filed for the purpose of obtaining a decree.
issues.conclusion: The award was not within the category of instruments requiring registration, so its lack of registration did not prevent a decree from being passed in its terms.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, registration is required for an instrument within its scope that creates or declares an interest in immovable property. The award did not itself create or declare such an interest.

predicates.arbitration_award_decree_proceeding: A party sought a court decree on an arbitration award.
predicates.award_preserves_existing_land_security: The award continued existing documents and securities relating to debts secured on land.
predicates.award_does_not_create_property_interest: The award stated the existing position concerning land rather than itself creating or declaring an interest in it.

issues.definition: When a decree is sought on an arbitration award that preserves existing land security without creating a property interest, the award requires no registration.

issues.legal_issue: A proceeding to obtain judgment and a decree on a filed arbitration award is not a suit requiring government consent to sue a ruler of a former state.
material_facts: The arbitrator filed the award in court, and the parties received notice of its filing.
The proceeding to obtain judgment and a decree on the award did not commence with a plaint or a petition in the nature of a plaint.
The party against whom the decree was sought was a ruler of a former Indian State, and the Central Government had not consented to the proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The court was competent to entertain the proceeding and pass a decree on the award without the Central Government's consent.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 86(1) and 87B of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 protect a ruler of a former Indian State from being sued without Central Government consent, but apply to suits. A proceeding under sections 14 and 17 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 to obtain judgment and a decree on an award is not a suit because it does not commence with a plaint or a petition in the nature of a plaint. Section 141 of the Code extends procedural provisions to other proceedings, not substantive immunity, and section 41(a) of the Arbitration Act does not extend the suit-specific protection to this proceeding. The Court relied on Province of Bombay v. K.S. Advani, Hansraj Gupta v. Official Liquidator, Dehra Dun-Mussorrie Electric Tramway Co., and Bhagwat Singh v. State of Rajasthan.

rule.if: arbitration_award_decree_proceeding and not proceeding_begun_by_plaint and respondent_is_former_state_ruler and government_consent_absent

predicates.arbitration_award_decree_proceeding: A party sought judgment and a decree in court on a filed arbitration award.
predicates.proceeding_begun_by_plaint: The proceeding commenced with a plaint or a petition in the nature of a plaint.
predicates.respondent_is_former_state_ruler: The person against whom the proceeding was brought was a ruler of a former state.
predicates.government_consent_absent: The government had not consented to the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a decree proceeding on a filed arbitration award was not begun by plaint, the respondent was a former-state ruler, and government consent was absent, the court may entertain the proceeding without that consent.

issues.legal_issue: A political privy-purse payment that is a political pension and is not legally enforceable in municipal courts is protected from attachment or sale in execution.
material_facts: The judgment debtor was entitled to periodic payments from the Government as a privy purse under a covenant associated with the integration of a former Indian State.
The payment obligation arose from political considerations and sanctions, and could not be enforced as a legal right in municipal courts.
A decree creditor sought attachment of the payments in execution of a decree.
issues.conclusion: The privy-purse payments were not liable to attachment or sale in execution of the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 60(1)(g) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 protects political pensions from attachment or sale in execution. The Court held that a privy purse paid periodically by the Government on political grounds, with an obligation not legally enforceable in municipal courts, has the essential characteristics of a political pension. It also held that the payment was not a debt or other property over which the recipient had disposing power under the main part of section 60(1). The Court relied on Nawab Bahadur of Murshidabad v. Karnani Industrial Bank Ltd. and Bishambhar Nath v. Nawab Imdad Ali Khan, and considered Articles 291 and 363 of the Constitution.

rule.if: execution_seeks_attachment_of_government_payment and payment_is_privy_purse and payment_is_periodic and payment_arises_from_political_obligation and not payment_is_legally_enforceable_in_municipal_court

predicates.execution_seeks_attachment_of_government: A decree creditor sought to attach a government payment to satisfy a judgment debt.
predicates.payment_is_privy_purse: The government payment was made to a ruler of a former state as a privy purse.
predicates.payment_is_periodic: The government made the payment periodically.
predicates.payment_arises_from_political_obligation: The payment obligation arose from political considerations and sanctions.
predicates.payment_is_legally_enforceable_in_munici: The recipient could enforce the payment as a legal right in a municipal court.

issues.definition: When execution seeks attachment of a periodic government privy-purse payment arising from a political obligation that cannot be enforced in a municipal court, the payment is protected from attachment or sale in execution.
